title: Signal condenser for noise-reduced oncall summaries and latency hinting
author: Maya R. Chen
release_notes: Add signal condenser utility to produce compact oncall summaries with priority stitching and latency hint recommendations; opt-in via slo-toolkit config and incident-bot mapping. Includes CLI and docs.
description:
Context & motivation: On-call noise from noisy alerts, repetitive traces, and noisy threshold breaches makes initial triage slow. This change introduces a standalone 'signal condenser' component in slo-toolkit that aggregates telemetry (alerts, SLO anomalies, sampled traces, and log fingerprints) into compact, prioritized on-call summaries and surface latency/throughput hints to guide responders. The condenser is tuned for high-noise services and supports TTL windows, dynamic priority stitching, and safe anonymization so teams can adopt it without exposing PII.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add condensed summary generator (src/condenser/signal_condenser.py) with a pluggable priority scoring pipeline (anomaly score, alert footprint, deployment impact, recent-change signal).
- Introduce sampling layer (cmd/slo_sampler) to emit representative telemetry bundles for downstream analysis and reduced-bandwidth oncall mailers.
- Integrate a new optional incident-bot hook (incident-bot/handlers/condenser_hook.py) to attach condensed snapshots to page events.
- Add a small CLI (bin/slo-condenser) for ops to run ad-hoc sampling and to produce JSON summaries for postmortems.
- Docs and quickstart (docs/oncall/signal-condenser.md) and runbook snippet templates used by incident-bot.

Commits (summary):
- Initial implementation of priority pipeline and condenser core (commit 1 of 4).
- Sampling CLI and incident-bot integration; feature flags and config (commit 2 of 4).
- Tests and fixtures for high-noise scenarios; add docs and examples (commit 3 of 4).
- Fix race in KV cache access, lint, and add ergonomics to CLI (commit 4 of 4).

Files changed (illustrative):
- src/condenser/signal_condenser.py (core algorithm + scoring pipeline)
- cmd/slo_sampler/__init__.py + cmd/slo_sampler/cli.py (sampling CLI)
- incident-bot/handlers/condenser_hook.py (optional hook to attach summaries to page events)
- docs/oncall/signal-condenser.md (how-to, config knobs, rollout guidance)
- tests/test_condenser.py (unit + integration tests with synthetic telemetry)
- charts/slo-toolkit/values.yaml (flag to enable hook in Helm deployments)

Behavioral notes & rollout plan:
- Default is opt-out: Helm values and runtime config must enable the incident-bot hook. The CLI and condenser can be used standalone by platform teams for postmortem sampling.
- Priority stitching can be customized per-service by injecting a small YAML mapping (docs includes example).
- The condenser respects a configurable TTL window (default 15m) and max bundle size to limit token/byte cost when summaries are attached to notifications.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests cover priority scoring permutations and anonymization; integration tests simulate bursty alert storms with synthetic traces.
- CI: lint -> unit -> integration -> acceptance. One flaky e2e (telemetry-sampler-acceptance) failed on first run due to test ordering; rerun passed. All checks green at merge.

Review thread (high-level):
- Omar Khanna (review): "Love the priority stitching idea. Two requests: make the default TTL configurable via env var and ensure the anonymizer is pluggable for regulated teams."
- Maya (author): "Done — added SLO_CONDENSER_TTL env var and an anonymizer interface with a noop adapter for teams that handle PII externally."
- Priya Patel (security review): "Please document threat model and data retention; confirm KMS usage for any persisted bundles."
- Maya: "Added docs section on data retention and confirmed condenser stores only hashed identifiers; no plaintext PII persisted. Helm values expose retention window; note added for KMS requirement when enabling persistent storage."
- Eliot Turner (ops review): "Minor: make CLI exit codes stable for automation and add a dry-run flag."
- Maya: "Added --dry-run and exit codes; updated tests. Thanks!"

Performance & safety:
- The scoring pipeline is intentionally cheap (O(n) across events in window) and limits memory by early eviction. Benchmarks: on a simulated noisy service (2k events/min) condenser CPU < 5% of a single c5.large equivalent and median end-to-end condensation latency ~120ms for a 15m window.
- Security: anonymization in the pipeline, optional KMS encryption for persisted bundles, and strict RBAC on incident-bot attachments. Docs include operational runbook for rollback and disabling the hook.

Migration & compatibility:
- No breaking API changes. The incident-bot hook is behind a feature flag. Existing oncall mailers will see no change unless enabled.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4981):
- Telemetry-driven threshold tuning (adaptive thresholds)
- UI integration in Redwood Console to preview condensed snapshots in alerts
- Export to downstream analysis pipelines and evaluation harness

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-14 after approvals from Omar, Priya, and Eliot. All CI green.

Notes for reviewers backporting: small config key added in charts/slo-toolkit/values.yaml (enableCondenser: false) — include in release branch if enabling feature flags for customers.

Contact: Maya R. Chen (author) for follow-ups and rollout assistance.
short_summary: Introduce a signal condenser in slo-toolkit that aggregates noisy telemetry into compact, prioritized oncall summaries; includes CLI, incident-bot hook, tests, and docs.
